title: Phasewise kernel blending and lightweight micro-probing for arch/seq-len autotune
creator: Leah Park
description: Implement an online autotuning system that blends kernel choices across prefill/decode phases using lightweight in-request micro-probes and a soft-bandit cost model, with architecture and sequence-length awareness. Goal is to reduce p95 latency while keeping token cost <= baseline and preserving model fidelity.
context: Current kernel selection uses static heuristics keyed by arch and coarse seqlen buckets. We've observed suboptimal choices for mixed workloads (long prefill, short decode) and heterogeneous GPUs. Need phase-aware decisions, cheaper probe budget, and safe fallback.
proposal: Build 'phasewise kernel blender' that: (1) assigns separate kernel candidate pools for prefill and decode, (2) runs tiny microbench probes on a small fraction of requests to update a lightweight cost/latency model, (3) uses a softmax-bandit with latency-cost constraints to pick kernels per request, (4) enforces safety by SLO-guarded fallback and conservative exploration scheduling per deployment.
acceptance_criteria: p95 end-to-end latency improvement >= 8% on mixed prefill/decode workloads in perf cluster A vs current baseline
token cost delta <= +1% (or decrease) measured over 7-day window on synthetic and real traffic replay
No regression in model output distribution (embedding cos-sim / generation logits sanity checks)
Rollout plan documented and feature-flagged with instant rollback
tasks: Run offline simulation against 14-day request logs to generate candidate kernel sets and initial cost priors (bench/data team)
Implement microprobe client (C++) that runs single-batch microbench on idle SMs with negligible interference
Add per-request context plumbing (phase, seqlen_histogram, arch_tag) to scheduler decision path
Build soft-bandit selector service with decay-based learning and constrained objective
Hook telemetry: per-kernel p50/p95 latency, queueing delay, tokens/sec, cost-estimates
Write E2E tests and reproducible harness (replay cluster)
Create canary rollout with gradual traffic % ramp and alerting (SLOs and cost)
PR + Code review + perf runs + docs
tradeoffs: Aggressive exploration may temporarily increase p95 and cost; microprobes consume a tiny GPU budget but could perturb tail latency if scheduled poorly. We trade immediate deterministic choices for better long-term adaptation to workload drift. Complexity increases runtime code-path and requires careful observability.
metrics_to_track: probe success rate and probe-induced latency delta
model fidelity metrics (embedding cosine similarity; LM perplexity proxy)
